specification.problem: Approximate Rz(theta) to operator-norm error epsilon (up to global phase) by a single-qubit Pauli+V circuit, using quaternion lattice enumeration with a sum-of-two-squares solve in place of a grid search. The abstract states only that the Ross-Selinger deterministic-search technique is adapted to Pauli+V with simple geometric methods; every equation below is background or an assumption.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance: single qubit, no black box, theta=pi/5 (assumed), epsilon about 0.3, small k (at most 3). Enumerate integer quaternions of norm 5^k near the target, reduce them to a V-word, and build the circuit. Outside scope: the paper's actual search algorithm, its proofs, its optimality and depth bounds, and any asymptotic claims.

equations.label: Quaternion to unitary
equations.latex: U_q=\frac{1}{5^{k/2}}\left(a I - i(b X + c Y + d Z)\right),\quad a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2=5^k
equations.description: A unit quaternion with denominator 5^{k/2} is a single-qubit SU(2) matrix. The coordinate-to-Pauli assignment is a convention; V=(I+2iX)/sqrt5 corresponds to 1+2i at k=1 (with sign convention -i X).
equations.justification: Standard quaternion-SU(2) correspondence. The sketch assumes the V gates are of this type.
assumptions: Sign and axis convention fixed here; the Pauli-conjugated V gates are the 1+-2i, 1+-2j, 1+-2k types

equations.label: Target rotation
equations.description: The target corresponds to the quaternion direction (cos(theta/2),0,0,sin(theta/2)), with the Z coefficient being d.

equations.label: Slab region
equations.description: Enumeration region in Z^4 for a level-k candidate. The sketch's sqrt(epsilon) bound on b,c is not a derived or established bound. Use the direct condition below as the actual acceptance test.
equations.justification: Heuristic region. The actual acceptance test is the operator-norm distance computed by simulation.
assumptions: Region bounds heuristic only; the final check is the explicit distance

equations.label: Two-squares residue
equations.description: For each candidate (a,d) in the sector, solve for (b,c). The residue is representable as a sum of two squares iff every prime p=3 mod 4 divides it to an even power. Solve via Gaussian-integer factorization, which is brute force at tiny sizes.
equations.justification: Classical number theory. The sketch's norm-equation approach is a proposal.
assumptions: Brute-force search over b,c is acceptable at small k

equations.label: Approximation criterion
equations.description: Verification in operator norm up to global phase. It is equivalent to a threshold on |Tr(R_z^\dagger U_q)|, i.e. |a cos(theta/2)+d sin(theta/2)|/5^{k/2}.
equations.justification: Error metric chosen in the sketch assumptions.

steps.description: Pick theta and epsilon. For k=0,1,2,... enumerate integer (a,d) with a^2+d^2<=5^k in the sector near 5^{k/2}(cos(theta/2),sin(theta/2)).
For each (a,d), solve b^2+c^2=5^k-a^2-d^2 (when nonneg and representable). Accept the first candidate meeting the error criterion, taking k minimal.

Reduce the quaternion to a word. Primitive reduction: if q is divisible by none of the 5 divisors (not divisible by an ideal above 5 beyond Pauli), peel off V-type factors (1+-2i, 1+-2j, 1+-2k) one at a time (by trial division in Hurwitz/Lipschitz quaternions) to get a length-k word, plus a Pauli (unit) factor. Alternative for tiny k: brute-force search over all reduced words of length k and compare to the target.

Build the single-qubit circuit by applying the V-word gates as unitary gates (e.g. from rx/rz/h compositions or U gates with the computed matrices) and Pauli gates (x,y,z). The gate order is the reverse of the matrix product order. No measurement; the statevector or unitary is read.

specification.classical_postprocessing: Classical enumeration, two-squares solve, quaternion factoring and word reduction as in the steps. Verify distance by simulating the unitary.
assumptions: The scope instance (theta, epsilon, k) is my choice
Unique reduced word via unique factorization is assumed. In Lipschitz/Hurwitz quaternions factorization is unique only up to units, so Pauli factors must be tracked
Implement V as exact Qiskit gates built from rx(-2*atan(2))-type rotations: V=(I+2iX)/sqrt5=Rx(-2 arctan 2). Pauli-conjugates are Ry and Rz of the same angle, and the inverses are the opposite angles
The expected depth about 3 log_5(1/epsilon) is an unverified heuristic from the sketch
missing_information: The paper's actual deterministic search procedure and its guarantees
Precise slab region and enumeration order
Handling of divisibility by 5 and the canonical normal form of words
